title: W_QK Effective Rank Measurement

secondary_analysis.note: No anti-correlation between per-head effective rank and delta within C-alien-rich

H_rank_ordered.notes: All corpora: mean_r_eff in [53.3, 58.0]. C-alien (53.3) < C-NAT-anon (58.0) technically holds but the 8% difference is not at the predicted scale. C-alien-rich (53.5) is not between them — it is equal to C-alien. Rank is effectively corpus-independent.

H_rank_S.notes: Ratio = 1.003. Far from the S-ratio prediction of 4.0. W_QK rank does not track world state-space dimension S.

H_rank_delta_correlated.criterion: Pearson r(R_eff, Delta_med) < -0.3 pooled across corpora

H_rank_backbone.notes: L0 r_eff in C-alien (56.6) is not lower than C-NAT-anon (58.2) by a meaningful margin. Backbone collapse is not explained by lower W_K rank in L0.

key_finding: W_QK effective rank (participation ratio) is corpus-independent: all corpora produce mean_r_eff ~53-58 out of max 64. The low-rank SYK mechanism at the W_QK level is not operative. HOWEVER: stable rank (R_stable) shows a real 1.8x difference between C-NAT-anon (15.8) and alien corpora (~8.8-9.0). This indicates a spectral concentration effect: alien corpora produce W_K with a few very dominant singular values; C-NAT-anon distributes energy more evenly. The participation ratio is insensitive to this; stable rank captures it.
implication: The relevant low-rank object in the SYK threshold derivation is NOT W_K itself but the INPUT-CONDITIONED ATTENTION KERNEL K(x_i, x_j) = x_i^T W_K^T W_Q x_j. Even a full-rank W_K produces a low-rank kernel when the input token distribution is concentrated (as in C-alien, where 8 world states produce clustered token representations). The correct next experiment: measure effective rank of the attention gram matrix on actual corpus tokens, not W_K in isolation.
